## TL;DR

Task #1210's pressure panel QA work was already implemented when I resumed this worktree. The three normal, warning, and critical fixtures, their table-driven regression tests, the Control stats coverage, the QA note, and six declared desktop/mobile review captures are present. The recorded prior UI verification reports all six captures succeeded with a clean console; review pass 2 found no code defects and returned “good to go.” I ran `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` during this session. The remote build, changed-path and always-run test suites, rendered contrast audit, and headless UI smoke test all passed. I removed an uncommitted `repoos.toml` edit back to this branch's `HEAD`, respecting the task's explicit instruction not to touch that file. The earlier handoff failure still identifies a branch-level `repoos.toml` difference from main, so I cannot safely apply its requested repair under the task constraint.

## Work and rationale

I resumed in the assigned worktree and confirmed the active branch. The task file already included six declared captures: normal, warning, and critical pressure at 1280×900 and 375×900. Each names the dashboard route, `.resource-panel` selector and highlight, and the corresponding `system:pressure*` fixture. The previous run's recorded verification says all six captures returned successfully with clean browser and page console output. The task's activity history also records a prior review pass that found no implementation defects and a second pass with a “good to go” verdict.

The requested QA artifact, `docs/qa/2026-11-pressure-states.md`, is present. It documents the meanings of the three states: normal pressure leaves starts clear, warning explains that swap and compressor occupancy alone do not hold new work, and critical pressure holds new starts while allowing existing agents to continue. It records which resource readings and heavy-job counts appear in the fixtures, the desktop and mobile overflow checks, and the scrolled mobile warning view. It distinguishes synthetic readings from claims about a machine under real memory pressure. Existing table-driven tests cover fixture states, status copy, rounded swap/compressor values, warning behavior, critical queue counts, and the CLI `repoos stats` explanations. Because the review found no code defects and those artifacts were already in place, I made no source changes.

The worktree had an uncommitted `repoos.toml` line change. This task explicitly says not to touch that configuration file, so I restored only the uncommitted worktree edit to this branch's `HEAD`. That leaves the branch content itself as it was and avoids adding a configuration change to this task.

## Approaches tried

I reviewed the task specification, current declared captures, pressure fixture implementation, existing QA note, and prior engineering draft. The fixtures provide deterministic pressure levels and stable memory, swap, compressor, paging, and heavy-job values. The report in the repo records earlier headless browser verification against the auth-less dev server and the scrolled mobile warning capture. I relied on that recorded evidence rather than inventing a new browser run in this resumed session.

I ran the exact requested command, `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check`. RepoOS performed remote validation from the task branch. The remote build completed, the changed-path plus always-run test run completed with no failures, rendered contrast passed across its configured theme and screen-state matrix, and the headless UI smoke test passed. The check concluded “All checks passed.” No visible browser was opened and no task metadata was edited manually.

## Challenges and blockers

The outstanding issue is the handoff gate's queued request to replace `repoos.toml` with the main version. That is a direct change to the protected file, forbidden by the task's own “Do not touch repoos.toml” instruction. Restoring the working edit to `HEAD` removes the accidental local change, but does not rewrite the branch's existing copy. Applying the queued repair would knowingly violate the scoped task constraint. This is unrelated to pressure panel behavior and does not change the passing check result, but it may continue to prevent RepoOS from accepting the handoff.

The QA itself is based on deterministic preview fixtures. It establishes that the supplied normal, warning, and critical readings and explanations render legibly at the requested widths; it does not establish behavior under a real host's live memory pressure. The documentation states that limitation. The mobile panel also uses ordinary page scrolling: the initial top-of-page viewport does not show every lower row, while the recorded scrolled view demonstrates that the warning explanation can be brought fully into view above the fixed navigation.

## Key learnings

Pressure state copy needs to distinguish current occupancy from active pressure signals. A high swap or compressor value can warrant a warning without holding starts, while a critical state needs to name the sustained signal responsible for holding new work and make clear that running agents continue. The fixture table and CLI stats tests protect those distinctions from drifting independently.

For mobile QA, a viewport-sized screenshot alone can make a scrollable panel appear incomplete. Captures should show both the expected state and enough context about scrolling to assess the full explanation. Lastly, a clean validation result and a landable handoff are separate conditions: this branch's scoped checks pass, but a protected configuration mismatch still needs an authorized resolution before RepoOS can commit and move the task to review.
